answer: Anchor standing to live, one-time exchanges: credit only work done inside timestamped multi-party conversations, where each participant keeps a mirror record of what was said. A zephyr of a moment, once it passes, cannot be replayed. A sybil farm can mint identities, but one operator cannot be attentively present in many simultaneous live exchanges, and forged presence fails when the independent mirror records disagree; the ferrous rule is that a record contradicting another participant's mirror earns no credit and taints the claimant, so faking presence costs more than earning it.
